title: Cognitive Load
summary: Cognitive load is the mental effort needed to understand, compare and act; review minimizes avoidable working-memory, decision and interpretation burden.

MUST.text: Externalize information users must compare or remember (e.g., keep selected plan and billing cadence visible during checkout).

SHOULD.text: Group options and reveal complexity progressively without hiding essentials.

AVOID.text: Do not claim a universal maximum number of options.

EXAMPLE.good: Checkout shows selected plan, price and renewal date on every step
EXAMPLE.bad: User must remember plan details from a previous page

FAILURE_MODES: Reducing visible options can increase load if labels become vague; test comprehension.
Progressive disclosure that hides required fields causes rework; keep essentials visible.
Memory aids such as tooltips add reading load; prefer inline clarity.
